newsitem.title: THAILAND: FOCUS-Thailand Alphatec invoved in huge deceit-CEO.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Thailand Alphatec invoved in huge deceit-CEO.

text.p: A huge fraud perpetrated through one of Thailand's leading industrial firms has led to discrepancies of around 10 billion baht ($322 million) at Alphatec Electronics Plc, excecutives said on Monday.
Auditors called in to sift through the firm's accounts found unauthorised transactions supported by falsified documents, the company's acting Chief Executive Officer Bob Mollersteun told reporters.
The company had also falsified profit figures released through the Stock Exchange of Thailand for at least three years, he said.
"There were some transactions with some external companies and it appears as though the transactions were incorrectly recorded to inflate the sales and profits of the company," Mollersteun said.
"There were I believe some fictional transactions...I believe there is some paperwork backing up some of these transactions," he added.

Auditors Price Waterhouse, called in by creditors earlier this year after 1996 year-end accounts were qualified, found evidence the firm had inflated its profits by around four billion baht in just over two years, Mollersteun said.
"The company reported profits in the first quarter of 1997 and in previous years that should have been represented as significant losses," he said.
"The amount of overstatement is not accurately defined but in the two years of 1995 and 1996 and the first quarter of 1997 it adds up to somewhere around four billion baht," he added.

Improper transactions between related companies within and outside the Alphatec Group were estimated to total a further six billion baht the Alphatec group, Mollersteun said. Most of this involved cash, Chief Financial Officer Leslie Merszei said.
Part of the the firm's estimated US$400 million dollars in total lending may have been improperly used, Merszei added.
Alphatec Electronics and its founder and former CEO Charn Usawachoke have been heralded as trailblazers in a drive to propel Thailand's growing electronics industry toward high technology production.
The firm, which packages semiconductors, has substantial facilities in the United States.
But it had run into trouble recently as Thailand endures its worst ever economic crisis and many sources of corporate funding have run dry for highly leveraged Thai firms.
Some Thai media reported that Charn had fled the country. Mollersteun said he remained in Bangkok.
Seven members of the firm's financial department were being investigated by the company though no criminal investigation was planned at this time, he said.
The auditors' findings had been anticipated and worked into a rescue plan for the company which still had solid fundamentals, Mollersteun said.

The firm was seeking an immediate 100-200 million baht emergency funding package from Thai banks but remained confident of its future. It had a solid and credible rescue plan to present to creditors on August 6, Mollersteun said. ($1 = 32 baht)
